_doc: THE WORN GROUND OF THE 1812 POTAWATOMI CAMP (T-3342, T-3511). One patch to each lodge_camp ground, worn round the lodges, fires and yards the archetype lays there, laid by renderers/web/js/yards.js as `worn_earth` and feathered into the sward. NOT ONE COORDINATE HERE IS AUTHORED - the rings are derived from the camp's sidecars in data/sidecars/1812/ by tools/generate_camp_ground_1812.py, and tools/check.sh re-derives this file byte for byte. IT DRAWS NO FENCE (`runs: []`). Every value is `reconstructed`; docs/LIBERTIES.md L-1812-potawatomi-camp-2515 states what bounds it.
name: The worn ground of the Potawatomi camp of August 1812
coordinates: Local East-North-Up metres from data/datum.json's origin - the frame the sidecars' placement.local_e / local_n use.

derived_from.note: Each ground's footprint, placement, counts and seed are its record's, and the archetype lays its lodges and yards from them; this layer adds only a reconstructed surface, worn round what the archetype lays, and its feather.

existence.note: That the camp stood on these grounds is the camp records' argument; that its ground was worn bare round the lodges and yards, fading raggedly into grass, is this project's reading of a camp lived in for days. docs/LIBERTIES.md L-1812-potawatomi-camp-2515.

runs_note: EMPTY, AND DELIBERATELY. A camp is not fenced; there is no run to draw.

ground.note: A working yard's treatment: bare dusty dirt with trampled grass surviving at its edges, the right reading for ground walked and worked between lodges.
ground.interior_drawn_within_note: T-3527: one entry to each ring above, in the same order: the days its camp stands, from that camp's record (documented_range with drawn_only_within), or null for a ground drawn every day. yards.js draws a ring's earth only on its days, as buildings.js draws the camp; on any other date the Season or a jaunt sets, the ground is the prairie's (the owner, 2026-11-08, chose that the camps come and go with the date).
ground.dwellings_note: T-3526: the plan of every lodge and bark house standing on these grounds, as [e, n, half_x, half_y, axis_deg, p] (centre, half-axes along and across the dwelling's own x axis, that axis counter-clockwise from east, superellipse exponent), read off the archetype's layout like the rings. yards.js leaves its earth out from under each, so the bare ground drawn over the terrain cannot paint over a lodge's foot from a distance (the owner, 2026-11-08: the mat lodges seemed to float above the ground from far away). Nothing here claims evidence; the lodges' own records do.
ground.fringe_note: Each patch is worn round its own camp's lodges and yards, so no two are the same shape, and feathers 5.0 m into the grass, a wandering fade rather than a line.

assertions.claim: every lodge_camp record drawn in 1812 has its worn patch
no two camp patches are the same shape: laid on each other by their middles, every pair differs somewhere by more than 1.5 m (T-3511: the owner saw fourteen alike)

research_note: WHAT WOULD MOVE THIS OFF RECONSTRUCTION: a description or picture of the camp's ground, or a plan of where its lodges stood. T-3511 (2026-11-08) checked the regular look the owner questioned: Currey's 'groups of Indian wigwams clustered along the creek' and the 1833 treaty witnesses in Andreas ('encamped on all sides ... beneath the low wood which chequered them', 'in groups in their wigwams scattered about on the prairie') describe groups, not rows or rounds, so each patch now follows its own group's lodges.
